question: Which of the following is an enzyme that is secreted in the stomach during the process of digestion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pepsin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pepsin** is a digestive enzyme that is secreted by the stomach, specifically from the gastric glands located in the lining of the stomach.
 
• Pepsin is secreted in an inactive form called **pepsinogen**. Pepsinogen is activated into pepsin by hydrochloric acid (HCl) present in the stomach.
 
• **Function of Pepsin:** It plays a critical role in breaking down proteins into smaller peptides during the process of digestion. Proteins are complex molecules, and pepsin facilitates their breakdown into more digestible forms.
 
• **Location:** Pepsin activity occurs in the highly acidic environment of the stomach, where the pH is around 1.5-3.5. This acidic condition is essential for its optimal functioning.
 
• **Importance:** Pepsin is one of the first enzymes to initiate the digestion of dietary proteins. Without it, protein digestion would be significantly impaired.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mucus:**

 
 
• Mucus is secreted by the stomach lining but it is not an enzyme. It serves as a protective layer to prevent the stomach lining from being damaged by the acidic gastric juice and digestive enzymes.
 
• Its primary function is protection rather than digestion.
 
 
 
• **Amylase:**
 
 
• Amylase is a carbohydrate-digesting enzyme that is secreted by the salivary glands and pancreas, not the stomach.
 
• It breaks down starch into simpler sugars like maltose.
 
• Amylase does not function in the acidic environment of the stomach. It is active in the mouth and small intestine.
 
 
 
• **Trypsin:**
 
 
• Trypsin is a protein-digesting enzyme secreted by the pancreas in an inactive form called trypsinogen.
 
• It becomes active in the small intestine and aids in further digestion of proteins after pepsin has initiated the process in the stomach.
 
• It does not play a role in digestion within the stomach.
 
 
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl):**
 
 
• HCl is secreted by the parietal cells in the stomach lining. It creates an acidic environment that is essential for the activation and functioning of pepsin.
 
• It helps in killing harmful bacteria present in food and denaturing proteins for easier digestion.
 
 
 
• **Protein Digestion:**
 
 
• The process of protein digestion starts in the stomach with pepsin and is completed in the small intestine with enzymes like trypsin and chymotrypsin.
 
• The breakdown of proteins is essential for the absorption of amino acids, which are the building blocks for various bodily functions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Stomach Enzymes:** The stomach primarily secretes pepsin for protein digestion, but it also produces other components like mucus and hydrochloric acid for maintaining digestion and protecting the stomach lining.
 
• **Pepsinogen Activation:** The activation of pepsinogen into pepsin is a self-regulating process that ensures enzyme activity occurs only when needed, preventing damage to the stomach lining.
 
• **pH Dependency:** Pepsin requires a very low pH to function effectively. This is why the stomach environment is highly acidic, maintained by hydrochloric acid secretion.
 
• **Role in Overall Digestion:** While pepsin works in the stomach, other enzymes like amylase and trypsin function in different parts of the digestive system, ensuring comprehensive digestion of food.
